da.text: From time to time, we may enter into business combinations. Business acquisitions are accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting, which allocates the fair value of the purchase consideration to the tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed based on their estimated fair values. In the fair value evaluation of intangible assets acquired, there are significant estimates and assumptions, including forecasts of future cash flows, revenues; and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization; as well as the selection of the royalty rates and discount rates. The excess of the purchase consideration over the fair values of these identifiable assets and liabilities is recorded as goodwill. The acquisition method of accounting also requires us to refine these estimates over a measurement period not to exceed one year to reflect new information obtained about facts and circumstances that existed as of the acquisition date that, if known, would have affected the measurement of the amounts recognized as of that date. If we are required to adjust provisional amounts that we have recorded for the fair values of assets and liabilities in connection with acquisitions, these adjustments could have a material impact on our financial condition and results of operations.

gp.heading: Gross Profit Margin
gp.text: Gross profit margin is calculated as net sales less cost of sales, divided by net sales, and increased in the current-year quarter compared to the prior-year quarter, due to higher gross profit margins in both segments. The increase was primarily driven by higher sales volume and favorable mix, partially offset by higher inventory step-up amortization related to the FGC acquisition.

cor.text: Gross profit margin is calculated as net sales less cost of sales, divided by net sales, and increased in the current-year quarter compared to the prior-year quarter, due to higher gross profit margins in both segments. The increase was primarily driven by higher sales volume and favorable mix, partially offset by higher inventory step-up amortization related to the FGC acquisition.

oi.heading: Segment Operating Margin
oi.text:
Diversified Industrial operating margin decreased by 40 basis points in the current-year quarter compared to the prior-year quarter. Within the North America businesses, segment operating margin decreased by 180 basis points, primarily driven by higher amortization expense of acquired intangibles, acquisition integration charges and amortization of step-up in inventory to fair value related to the acquisition of FGC, partially offset by higher sales volume, favorable product mix and pricing. Within the International businesses, segment operating margin increased by 160 basis points, primarily due to higher sales volume, favorable product mix and pricing, partially offset by higher amortization expense of acquired intangibles and amortization of step-up in inventory to fair value related to the acquisition of FGC.

We expect to incur approximately $75 million and $35 million in business realignment and acquisition integration charges, respectively, during the remainder of fiscal 2027. Continually changing business conditions could impact the ultimate costs we incur.

ga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses ("SG&A") increased in the current-year quarter compared to the prior-year quarter, primarily due to incremental SG&A costs associated with the acquisition of FGC, higher intangible asset amortization and higher acquisition-related transaction costs. To a lesser extent, the current-year quarter was also impacted by higher acquisition integration expenses and higher R&D expenses.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses ("SG&A") increased in the current-year quarter compared to the prior-year quarter, primarily due to incremental SG&A costs associated with the acquisition of FGC, higher intangible asset amortization and higher acquisition-related transaction costs. To a lesser extent, the current-year quarter was also impacted by higher acquisition integration expenses and higher R&D expenses.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense increased during the current-year quarter compared to the prior-year quarter, primarily due to higher average debt outstanding.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The effective tax rate for both the current-year and prior-year quarters was greater than the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% due to foreign tax effects and state and local income taxes net of federal benefit, which were partially offset by tax benefits from the foreign-derived deduction eligible income and stock-based compensation. Additionally, the current-year quarter tax rate was impacted by other one time discrete tax costs.

The fiscal 2027 effective tax rate is expected to be approximately 22.5%.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities decreased $30 million in the current-year quarter compared to the prior-year quarter. The decrease was primarily driven by increased working capital requirements within accounts receivable and inventory and higher income taxes paid, partially offset by higher net income adjusted for non-cash items (including depreciation, amortization, stock-based compensation expense and deferred income taxes). Cash flows from operating activities in the current-year quarter were also negatively impacted by acquisition-related transaction costs of $55 million. We continue to focus on managing inventory and other working capital requirements.

wc.text: Net cash provided by operating activities decreased $30 million in the current-year quarter compared to the prior-year quarter. The decrease was primarily driven by increased working capital requirements within accounts receivable and inventory and higher income taxes paid, partially offset by higher net income adjusted for non-cash items (including depreciation, amortization, stock-based compensation expense and deferred income taxes). Cash flows from operating activities in the current-year quarter were also negatively impacted by acquisition-related transaction costs of $55 million. We continue to focus on managing inventory and other working capital requirements.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: We are targeting 2.5% of sales for capital expenditures for fiscal 2027 and have an annual long-term target of 2.0%. We will continue to prioritize capital expenditures related to safety, productivity and strategic investments.

net sales.heading: Net Sales
net sales.text:
Throughout this discussion, both reported sales growth, determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP, and organic sales growth, a non-GAAP measure, are presented. Organic sales growth represents the percentage change in net sales adjusted to exclude the effects of acquisitions and divestitures for the twelve-month period following their completion, as well as the impact of changes in currency exchange rates. Management believes these adjustments provide management and investors with additional insight into underlying sales trends and facilitate meaningful period-to-period comparisons of operating performance. References to organic sales in this discussion reflect this measure and are presented as a percentage increase or decrease relative to the comparable prior-year period. Total Company net sales changed as follows:

Net sales in the current-year quarter increased by $908 million, or 17.9%, compared to the prior-year quarter, primarily due to higher organic sales in both segments and incremental sales associated with the FGC and Curtis acquisitions. Incremental net sales from acquisitions were approximately $349 million in the current-year quarter. These changes are discussed in more detail within the business segment results section below.

intro.text: Parker-Hannifin Corporation was incorporated in Ohio in 1938. As used in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, unless the context otherwise requires, the terms "Company", "Parker", "we" or "us" refer to Parker-Hannifin Corporation and its subsidiaries, and the term "year" and references to specific years refer to the applicable fiscal year. Parker is a global leader in motion and control technologies. Leveraging a unique combination of interconnected technologies, we design, manufacture, and provide aftermarket support for highly engineered solutions that create value for customers primarily in aerospace & defense, in-plant & industrial equipment, transportation, off-highway, energy, and HVAC & refrigeration markets around the world.

oi.heading: Segment Operating Margin
oi.text:
Diversified Industrial segment operating margin increased by 100 basis points in 2026 compared to 2025. Within the North America businesses, segment operating margin increased by 110 basis points in 2026 compared to 2025, primarily driven by favorable pricing and benefits from prior year divestitures, partially offset by unfavorable product mix, increased material costs and higher intangible amortization. Within the International businesses, segment operating margin increased by 90 basis points in 2026 compared to 2025, primarily driven by favorable mix and pricing, partially offset by higher business realignment charges.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense in 2026 decreased compared to 2025 primarily due to lower average rates on commercial paper borrowings.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The effective tax rate in 2026 was lower than the U.S. Federal statutory rate of 21% due to share-based compensation, foreign-derived intangible income and U.S. Federal income tax credits, which were partially offset by U.S. state and local taxes and tax effects in foreign jurisdictions.

The effective tax rate in 2025 was lower than the U.S. Federal statutory rate of 21% due to tax benefits from the release of a foreign valuation allowance, share-based compensation, foreign-derived intangible income and a tax benefit from a lower taxable gain on divestitures than gain under GAAP, which were partially offset by U.S. state and local taxes and taxes related to international activities.

Refer to Note 5 to the consolidated financial statements for a further reconciliation of the U.S. federal statutory tax rate to our effective tax rate.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities increased $588 million in 2026 compared to 2025. The increase was primarily driven by higher net income adjusted for non-cash items (including depreciation, amortization, stock-based compensation expense, deferred income taxes and gains on sale of businesses), which more than offset the increased working capital requirements, specifically within inventory and accounts receivable. We continue to focus on managing inventory and other working capital requirements.

da.text: From time to time, we may enter into business combinations. Business acquisitions are accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting, which allocates the fair value of the purchase consideration to the tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed based on their estimated fair values. In the fair value evaluation of intangible assets acquired, there are significant estimates and assumptions, including forecasts of future cash flows, revenues; and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization; as well as the selection of the royalty rates and discount rates. The excess of the purchase consideration over the fair values of these identifiable assets and liabilities is recorded as goodwill. The acquisition method of accounting also requires us to refine these estimates over a measurement period not to exceed one year to reflect new information obtained about facts and circumstances that existed as of the acquisition date that, if known, would have affected the measurement of the amounts recognized as of that date. If we are required to adjust provisional amounts that we have recorded for the fair values of assets and liabilities in connection with acquisitions, these adjustments could have a material impact on our financial condition and results of operations.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Other receivables
lines.why: Owed by suppliers and others, not by customers (vendor non-trade receivables): operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Total assets and total revenue that were excluded from management's assessment represented approximately 4% and 1%, respectively, of consolidated total assets and net sales, as of and for the year ended June 30, 2026.
We do not depend on any single patent, trademark, copyright, trade secret or license or group of patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets or licenses to any material extent.

We depend on the skills, institutional knowledge, working relationships, and continued services and contributions of key personnel, including our leadership team, engineers and others at all levels of the company, as a critical part of our human capital resources.
In addition, our ability to achieve our operating and strategic goals depends on our ability to identify, hire, train and retain qualified individuals.

Over the long term, the extent to which our business and results of operations will be impacted by global economic and political uncertainty and geopolitical risks depends on future developments that remain uncertain.
